note: Reel 35: You're the Cashier. Episode 10 of 'You're the test subject'. A man robs your counter at knifepoint; you can't pick his face from the line, but you pick his knife at once. Script v3, after two cold reads and a script review: the guilt lands before the answer, as a question true for every pick (n07); nobody who refused to pick wins (n10, over the empty doorway, not his card); the science gives the result in natural frequencies, one in three and one in seven (n14, n14b); the last question challenges the people who got him (n15, n16); the dare is cut. The narrator is the series voice (af_heart). The robber is am_michael (clean on short lines with an exclamation mark, reels 27, 28, 30). Facts: docs/research.md. Read audio/vo_lab/takes/phonemes.md after every run (watch 'drawer': misaki made 'drawing' one syllable in reel 30).
ref_text: The night was cold and very quiet. Most of the street was asleep, and the lamps hummed over the empty road. Somewhere far away, a train rolled past, and then the silence came back.

lines.text: You're the cashier, and he's got a knife.
Whoever you pick goes to jail.
But the knife doesn't go to jail.
Were you that sure of the man you sent to jail?
Picked nobody? He's still out there.
You just sent an innocent man to jail.
In the classic test, one in three picked the right man.
With a gun, one in seven.
Then who else was in the shop?
